title: Most stable cell groupings spread contacts evenly; unstable ones concentrate them

fields.label: Label
fields.value: Most stable cell groupings spread contacts evenly; unstable ones concentrate them

fields.label: Statement
fields.value: Among the possible arrangements of a small group of cells, the most stable (and therefore commonest) are those in which the cell-to-cell contacts are most evenly divided among the cells, and the least stable are those in which one cell has a predominant number of contacts.

fields.label: Chapter
fields.value: Ch. VIII: The Forms of Tissues, or Cell-Aggregates (continued)

fields.label: Quotation
fields.value: But it would appear that the most stable arrangements are those in which the total number of contacts is most evenly divided, and the least stable are those in which some one cell has, as in type _f_, a predominant number of contacts.

fields.label: Agent
fields.value: delphisci On Growth and Form claim extractor

fields.label: Assumptions
fields.value: D’Arcy Wentworth Thompson, On Growth and Form (1st ed., Cambridge: Cambridge University Press, 1917), Chapter VIII, “The Forms of Tissues, or Cell-Aggregates (continued)”; topic “Stability of eight-cell arrangements”. Scope: small aggregates of cells or drops (segmenting eggs, oil-drop models)

fields.label: Assessment
fields.value: GPT-5.6 Sol on thompson1917-ch08-10: partially-resolvable, resolvability 0.65

fields.label: Finding
fields.value: Contact inequality and persistence are measurable, but stability has several possible operational definitions. Existing time series can test association in model systems, while causal attribution and the broad class of oil-drop models remain incomplete.

fields.label: Proposed test in the assessment
fields.value: Proposed test with existing data: For observed small-cell contact graphs, calculate inequality of contact counts and test whether low-inequality topologies persist longer or occur more frequently than concentrated-contact topologies.

fields.label: Evidence against
fields.value:
Lineage programs and sampling can determine topology prevalence.

Frequency is not identical to mechanical stability.

fields.label: Finding
fields.value: Evenness of contacts and the frequency of each arrangement are both countable from cleavage volumes, and their correlation is a real prediction. The volumes are not a balanced sample across the types, and frequencies have not been deposited. A biased atlas can support a partial test and cannot yet establish which arrangements are the commonest in nature.

fields.label: Proposed test in the assessment
fields.value: Proposed test with existing data: Rank eight-cell and similar small aggregates by how evenly contacts are distributed among the cells, and compare that rank with how often each arrangement occurs. Frequency falling as contact variance rises would support the claim; common arrangements in which one cell takes most of the contacts would refute it.

fields.label: Evidence against
fields.value:
Published figures over-sample arrangements authors considered normal, which can fake a stability ranking.

Oil-drop models mentioned alongside cells are not part of these biological archives.
